grading: Each criterion is pass/fail with a quoted response excerpt. Fatal errors fail the case. A case passes only if all criteria pass and no fatal error occurs. Grade only the requested issue, not incidental formatting. Keep this file hidden from evaluated agents.

criteria: Keep async/await; identify the Chromium-only scope if discussing the prohibition.
Do not recommend a runtime migration or GN/Chromium layout.
fatal_errors: Removes or prohibits async outside Chromium.

criteria: Accept justified Arc sharing and distinguish pointer cloning from deep cloning.
Do not introduce per-worker deep copies or remove required cross-thread sharing.
fatal_errors: Treats Arc or Arc::clone as categorically prohibited.

criteria: Keep the slice/Vec API given known application consumers.
Avoid mandatory IntoIterator/impl Iterator/Into generalization.
fatal_errors: Demands a generic or iterator-return API despite the stated use.

criteria: Recommend &str because only borrowed string contents are needed.
Keep a borrow; do not add allocation or take ownership unnecessarily.
fatal_errors: Retains &String without justification or requires owned String.

criteria: Recommend Result and propagation/handling of the I/O error.
Explain that replacing unwrap with expect would still panic on recoverable input.
fatal_errors: Offers only unwrap-to-expect as the fix.

criteria: Permit an invariant panic and recommend expect with a reason, or remove the unnecessary panic by a clear equivalent implementation.
Do not require Result solely because a panic exists.
fatal_errors: Requires all panics be converted to Result.

criteria: Preserve public-field struct-update construction and Default.
Do not add non_exhaustive; recognize the options-struct exception.
fatal_errors: Adds non_exhaustive or privatizes fields breaking specified callers.

criteria: Recommend non_exhaustive on evolving cross-team Event.
Keep the stable two-state Visibility exhaustive; explain the difference.
fatal_errors: Applies non_exhaustive to both indiscriminately or misses Event.

criteria: Replace the production std::collections glob with explicit imports.
Allow use super::* in inline tests and the local enum glob.
fatal_errors: Flags every wildcard as forbidden without exceptions.

criteria: Respect stable and the existing width; unsupported formatter options may be omitted.
Do not install nightly, prescribe all-features unconditionally, or claim fmt/Clippy prove all style rules.
fatal_errors: Requires nightly or overwrites existing formatter configuration.

criteria: Identify undefined behavior for an empty slice.
Prefer a safe design such as first().copied() returning Option<u8>; comments alone do not fix soundness.
fatal_errors: Only adds a SAFETY comment or asserts the existing function is sound.

criteria: Keep inherent methods; do not create a trait just for organization.
Do not impose additional architecture beyond the stated need.
fatal_errors: Introduces a trait solely to organize methods.

criteria: Flag async/await and direct std thread spawning as Chromium-specific policy issues.
Refer to repository task/sequence infrastructure without inventing function names.
fatal_errors: Treats this as ordinary Cargo and approves both prohibited patterns.

criteria: Honor explicit local direct-function-import policy and explain the Google preference as a conflict.
Do not rewrite configuration or unrelated layout.
fatal_errors: Rewrites the direct import despite explicit project policy.

criteria: Use LANGUAGES.get(language), or equivalent Python lookup.
Do not activate/apply Rust guidance or convert the task to Rust.
fatal_errors: Applies the Rust style workflow to the Python task.
